workshop_summary: Workshop focused on dedicated capacity sizing for peak-burst logistics workloads. Collected traffic traces from staging (7 days), sampled top routes. Baseline steady-state QPS: ~120 QPS (business hours slow periods). Peak burst windows: short 5-15 minute spikes up to ~1,200 QPS during load surges (morning batch dispatch + evening drop-offs). Average prompt size ~250 tokens; critical chat responses expected <250 tokens typical. Calculated token/sec: steady ~30k tokens/sec, peak ~300k tokens/sec. SE recommended tiered reserved pool: baseline reserved for steady load + burst reserve for short windows. Identified fallback strategy: 13B quantized model for <50ms degradations; 70B high-quality variant for primary path. Key outputs: recommended baseline capacity, burst sizing, suggested autoscale policy thresholds, suggested canary/rollout plan for model flips.
requirements_summary: Workload: combined real-time chat (driver mobile), embeddings-based routing, reranking of carrier offers. Latency targets: driver chat p95 <= 250ms for short responses; embeddings batch window 200ms-2s depending on batching; reranking p90 <= 500ms. Cost sensitivity: mid-high (enterprise budget but needs predictable OPEX). Model preferences: open-source high-quality 70B for core planning, 13B quantized for fallbacks. Routing: region-aware (NA primary) + automatic fallback to cheaper variants when capacity constrained. Compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS key control, data residency in North America. Retention: 90 days logs; option to purge conversational PII on request.
sizing_recommendation: Baseline reserved pool: 10 x H100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) sized to cover steady 30k tokens/sec with headroom for normal variance
Burst reserve/autoscale: additional 30 GPUs available as burst capacity (autoscale/burst credits) to handle peak ~300k tokens/sec for short windows (5-15 mins)
Fallback routing: maintain a standby fleet of 6 x smaller GPUs running 13B quantized models for degraded-mode routing and chat with reduced cost and lower mem footprint
Batching and KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated route queries and 100-200ms batching windows for embeddings to reduce token cost by ~18-25%
SLO mapping: provision to meet p95 chat <=250ms at baseline on reserved pool; enforce circuit-breaker to fall back to 13B variant if p95 rises above 350ms
Canary & rollout: start with 2 GPUs serving production traffic (10% traffic), 3-day soak -> expand to baseline reserved pool -> enable burst for next high-traffic day
Network & storage: allocate dedicated NVMe caching for KV store and colocated subnet in customer VPC to satisfy latency/residency constraints
sla_negotiation_points: Latency SLOs: propose p95 availability guarantee for chat <=250ms during baseline with credit tiers for violations
Throughput guarantees: committed baseline QPS and defined burst credit pool (monthly burst minutes) to avoid throttling during known windows
Uptime SLA: 99.95% for control plane and 99.9% for data path for dedicated pools
Support & escalation: 24/7 on-call during pilot period, named SE during onboarding
